versions.short: The bill would direct the Department of Veterans Affairs to run two grant programs aimed at treating chronic mild traumatic brain injury in veterans, focusing on non-drug and newer therapies. The first would fund eligible nonprofits, academic institutions, and healthcare providers to design and test treatments and measure their effects on mental health, suicide risk, and long-term brain injury effects, with grants capped at $5,000,000 per year per recipient. The second would fund research and pilot studies through an independent outside organization, with a required annual report to Congress. The bill would also authorize $10,000,000 per year for fiscal years 2026 through 2028 for each program, end both programs three years after enactment, and extend the date in certain VA housing loan fee rules from June 9, 2034 to July 14, 2034.
